chunks: My group of scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Qasīm ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said:

‘Umar (‘Amr) ibn Yazīd came to me and said, “Ride.” So I rode with him, and we traveled until we arrived at the house of Ḥafs Al-Kunāsi. He brought him out, and he rode with us. We traveled until we arrived in Gharī, and we reached a grave. He said, “Come down! This is the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him).” We asked him, “From where do you know this?” He said, “I came to it with Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) when he was in Ḥīrah more than once, and he informed me that it is his grave.”
ai.seo_question: Who identified the grave of Imam Ali in Gharī and how did he know?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the reliability of the Qarqaniyyun and other companion chains in preserving the precise location of Imam Ali’s grave in Gharī, near Kufa. It underscores the Shia scholarly tradition of verifying sacred sites through direct transmission from the Imams, specifically linking the knowledge of the burial place to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) during the period of the Imams' residence in al-Hirah.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. All of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Qasīm ibn Muḥammad, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said:

One day ‘Umar ibn Yazīd came to me and asked me to accompany him. I joined him and we traveled until we arrived at the house of Ḥafs Al-Kunāsi. ‘Umar ibn Yazīd asked Ḥafs to join us also, and he did. We traveled until we arrived in Gharī. We arrived at a grave, (at which point) ‘Umar (ibn Yazīd) said, “Come down from your sumpters! This is the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).” We asked him, “How do you know this?” ‘Umar replied, “I came here with Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) more than once when he was in Ḥīrah, and he told me that this is the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).”
